claims.statement: DailyMed identifies Mounjaro as tirzepatide injection indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in label-specified type 2 diabetes populations. On 2026-08-28, FDA additionally approved Mounjaro to reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (CV death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or non-fatal stroke) in adults with type 2 diabetes at high cardiovascular risk, based on the SURPASS-CVOT trial; this expanded indication is reflected in Lilly's approval announcement and had not yet propagated to the DailyMed label text as of this review.

context.population: label-specified patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, including adults with T2D at high cardiovascular risk

extractedEvidence.quote: MOUNJARO is a glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) receptor and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control

Eli Lilly and Company (NYSE: LLY) today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Mounjaro (tirzepatide), a dual GIP and GLP-1 hormone receptor agonist, to lower the risk of major adverse cardiovascular (CV) events (MACE), including CV death, non-fatal heart attack, or non-fatal stroke in adults with type 2 diabetes who are at high risk for these events.

claims.statement: DailyMed tirzepatide product labels list personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2 as a contraindication. This boxed warning is based on rodent carcinogenicity studies; the label states it is unknown whether tirzepatide causes thyroid C-cell tumors, including MTC, in humans, as the human relevance of the rodent findings has not been determined.

context.population: patients with personal or family history of MTC or MEN 2

extractedEvidence.quote: Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or in patients with Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2

Tirzepatide causes thyroid C-cell tumors in rats. It is unknown whether MOUNJARO causes thyroid C-cell tumors, including medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), in humans as the human relevance of tirzepatide-induced rodent thyroid C-cell tumors has not been determined.

reviewFlags: independently corroborated (droracle.ai clinical-reference summary); rodent-study basis of the boxed warning added per reviewer note to avoid implying a demonstrated human carcinogenicity signal

claims.statement: FDA determined the tirzepatide shortage was resolved (December 19, 2024) and formally ended compounding enforcement discretion for tirzepatide: state-licensed (503A) compounders were required to stop by February 18, 2025, and outsourcing facilities (503B) by March 19, 2025. As of FDA's April 2026 restatement of this policy, mass/routine compounding of tirzepatide as an essentially-a-copy product is generally not permitted absent documented patient-specific necessity; compounded tirzepatide is not a routinely FDA-tolerated alternative to approved Mounjaro/Zepbound products, and BioStack should separate approved tirzepatide labels from compounded or vendor-marketed products.
